what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/publish-articles: the published articles of a pursuit, their feed, and the plans for a double opt-in newsletter signup.

payload.label: Read the published articles
payload.job: List the published articles of my pursuit, newest first
payload.description: Answers the cards (slug, title, description, category, published_at) of the articles of the pursuit database named by database whose status is published and whose published date has passed and that are listed, newest first, at most limit (100 when absent). A draft is never answered. The answer is the props of show/ArticleList.tsx.

database.description: The name of the pursuit database to read, bound by the trusted caller. The engine opens it with the login its vault holds as that name and -connection; no caller supplies a login.

limit.description: At most this many articles (100 when absent).

use.description: The use this statement runs for: a recipe step's declared purpose and surface (config.context.use, set by the workflow engine over any use the step's input carried). Given with database, the computer opens the database with its reader login (one that cannot get round the row rules, change a table or read the use binding) instead of the owner's, and hands the run a ticket of this use that it signed; the statement's transaction claims it first, so the database's row rules read this use and the statement cannot change it. A use with credential_name, which has no ticket, is refused. Absent: the owner's own work, read under the database's own purpose_when_unstated.

purpose.description: The purpose path, such as publish or coach/review.

surface.description: The surface path, such as social/instagram; empty for any surface.

provenance.source: Written in tools/publish-articles/do-work from the article and signup rules of tools/serve-articles-and-signup; read through run-sql-in-my-database/do-work/serve-a-read.ts

payload.label: Read a published article
payload.job: Read one published article with its sections, sources, related articles and course
payload.description: Answers the article named by slug when it is published: its title, description, category, picture, sections (the stored sections, else the markdown turned into sections of paragraphs and lists), short version, sources, the published articles it names as related, and the course it points to with its call to action. A draft or unknown slug answers article: null. The answer is the props of show/Article.tsx.

payload.label: Read the articles feed
payload.job: Make the RSS 2.0 feed of my published articles
payload.description: Answers xml: an RSS 2.0 feed of the newest 50 published articles of the pursuit database named by database, each linked at channel.origin plus the articles path (channel.articles_path, /articles when absent) and its slug. Every value is escaped. channel.origin must be an https origin with no path.

payload.label: Plan a newsletter signup
payload.job: Plan the double opt-in of one address: what to keep and the one confirmation message
payload.description: Reads the address's subscriber row and answers the plan: action send_confirmation with statements (for tool:run-sql-in-my-database) that keep the address as pending with only a digest of its confirmation token, and the one message (to, subject, text with the confirmation link) for tool:send-an-email; already_confirmed (nothing to write or send); or refused with the reason. Nothing is written or sent here, and nobody is sent anything but the confirmation until the link is opened.

database.description: The name of the pursuit database to read, bound by the trusted caller. The engine opens it with the login its vault holds as that name and -connection; no caller supplies a login.

source_path.description: The page the address was given on.

consent_text.description: The exact wording shown beside the form.

confirm_origin.description: The https origin the confirmation link points to.

payload.label: Plan a newsletter confirmation
payload.job: Decide what opening a confirmation link does
payload.description: Reads the subscriber named by id and answers confirm with the one statement that confirms it (the row must be pending, the token must match its stored digest and the link must be at most 48 hours old), already_confirmed, or invalid. The statement is run with tool:run-sql-in-my-database.
